title: Emmet Fox's Sermon on the Mount
baseline: fox.html and js/fox.js were clean at assignment start. Captured HEAD copies before edits; their content matched the working-tree baseline. Other dirty files were left untouched.
word_count_method: Text in main before sources, including headings, authored gallery cards, citations and captions; excludes hero, source section, navigation, styles and scripts. Word tokens retain internal apostrophes and hyphens. The authored gallery is counted once, not again after JavaScript renders it.
read_time_method: Narrative including all three gallery passages, rounded up at 200 words per minute; source list excluded.
editorial_rationale: Replaced the AA anecdote and promotional sermon framing with the concrete claim that inheriting the earth means dominion over health and circumstances. The post now introduces Fox as a religious interpreter whose claims readers can examine.

Preserved spiritual laws, mental causation, the possibility of beginning again, meekness, nonresistance, realization, the Golden Key and early AA readership. Added the distinction between goodwill and forced affection in forgiveness, which the old prayer-machine account obscured.

Rebuilt the three-card gallery around the Gospel passage, Fox's reading, and the interpretive step that connects them. All gallery summaries and lesson lines are explicitly labeled paraphrases in both HTML and generated JavaScript.

Removed the most-popular-preacher superlative, unaudited audience count, engineering jokes, compulsory contrasts, Sunday-school ridicule, stage directions, repeated callouts and the keep/drop checklist.

Removed The Secret and bestseller genealogy, Ehrenreich's breast-cancer statistic, and the Epictetus family tree. Those detours supplied a tidy modern lineage without doing the work needed to establish one.
Moved AA before the final limits section. The narrative now ends on the difficulty of identifying a failed fair trial when Fox explains failure through the reader's consciousness.
Kept the existing hero and structural classes, image assets, picture wrappers, gallery navigation, authored no-JavaScript cards and endcap. Root owns shared styling and visual QA.

major_factual_corrections.before: The Sermon was presented as a manual of practical psychology instead of moral demands, with Fox's account treated as the original meaning of Jesus.
major_factual_corrections.after: Fox's metaphysical reading is attributed to him. The meekness and nonresistance cards show where he adds definitions or moves instructions about conduct into thought. His ethical demand for forgiveness remains visible.

major_factual_corrections.before: The kingdom of heaven is within you was treated as a line from the Sermon.
major_factual_corrections.after: Removed this conflation. The phrase belongs to the interpretation of Luke 17:21, not Matthew's Sermon, and the usual wording names the kingdom of God.

major_factual_corrections.before: Daily bread was said to have nothing to do with food.
major_factual_corrections.after: Fox explicitly includes food and material needs before extending bread to a firsthand experience of divine presence.

major_factual_corrections.before: The Lord's Prayer was called a machine engineered by Jesus and a treatment that reliably changes the user.
major_factual_corrections.after: Explained Fox's religious interpretation of divine parenthood, realization and forgiveness without treating the prayer as a validated device.

major_factual_corrections.before: The Golden Key was declared sound because you cannot think about two things at once, with God optional and a direct parallel to therapy.
major_factual_corrections.after: Removed the cognitive claim and efficacy guarantee. Explained Fox's belief that an omnipotent God acts through prayer; stripping out God changes his proposed explanation. Possible reassurance is distinguished from external control.

major_factual_corrections.before: CBT and New Thought were described as parallel descendants of Epictetus, with CBT validating Fox's mechanism.
major_factual_corrections.after: No unsupported descent claim remains. The Beck Institute is cited for evaluation of thoughts, problem solving and behavior practice, which cannot prove Fox's universal metaphysical law.

major_factual_corrections.before: Early AA used Fox as its first textbook, and detailed claims about the authorship of God as we understood Him were asserted without primary evidence.
major_factual_corrections.after: AA's own archives publish Dorothy and Bill's 1954 recollection of popular early reading. The post names the recollection's scope and other reading, and does not infer official textbook status or authorship of the Steps.

major_factual_corrections.before: The medical critique used an unsourced breast-cancer mortality generalization and broad slogans about thought moving matter.
major_factual_corrections.after: The National Cancer Institute supports the specific limit: attitude is not convincingly linked to cancer risk or death. The page does not advise replacing medical care with prayer.

major_factual_corrections.before: The source note claimed a Grosset and Dunlap reprint while its Internet Archive link identifies a 1989 Perennial Library edition.
major_factual_corrections.after: Named the actually inspected 2010 HarperCollins digital text; the Archive link is described as an edition record, with a separate preview for the digital edition.

sources.type: AA General Service Office Archives newsletter and transcript
sources.verified: Downloaded original after web open returned an internal error. Page 2 reproduces the 1954 conversation with Bill W. and Dorothy, wife of Clarence S. sources.verified: CBT examines distressing thoughts, evaluates realism, teaches skills and includes problem solving and behavioral work. The model links interpretation with reactions, not external-event causation.
sources.limits: Not used to claim that Fox's practice is tested, or to rank all psychotherapies.

sources.verified: No convincing evidence connects attitude to developing or dying from cancer; support and activity can help coping.
sources.limits: Specific cancer claim, not a claim that stress or psychological processes have no influence on any aspect of health.

remaining_uncertainties: No original 1931 Golden Key printing was inspected; modern reprints differ in wording. The retained short quotation matches the identified reprint.
No facsimile of the 1934 Sermon first edition was inspected; claims are checked against the 2010 digital text, whose copyright page preserves the early dates.
The AA record establishes retrospective recollection of early readership. Its reach and contribution to sobriety cannot be measured from that transcript.
Possible reassurance from prayer is identified as a possibility for a believer, not as a measured effect of Fox's method.
No direct Fox-to-CBT or Fox-to-Step-wording lineage is asserted. The old historical claims were removed instead of being converted into another tidy genealogy.
suggested_hub_description: Fox reads Jesus's sermon as a method of spiritual healing. Early AA members valued the book; his promise that thought controls circumstances needs a separate judgment.
